meta.title: Fly Radio
meta.description: A radio station played by a real 166,700-neuron fruit-fly connectome, running live in your browser. Four shows, five flies, nothing pre-rendered or looped.

head.title: Fly Radio
head.lede: Four shows, five flies, the real 166,700-neuron connectome, running live in your browser. Every buzz you hear is that brain's own wing-motor-neuron activity, played the instant it's measured — nothing pre-rendered, nothing looped.

unit.label: Radio
unit.scene: A fly sitting at a desk, talking into a microphone

captions.label: Live translation
captions.title: Translation — live decoded reading
captions.before: Captions appear once you've tuned in.
captions.listening: Listening. The first reading comes after a second of the show.

note: Every buzz above is real: the amplitude comes straight from the actual 166,700-neuron MaleCNS connectome, downloaded once (58 MB, the same files as the Simulation) and stepped live on your device — specifically each cast member's own wing-motor-neuron spikes above rest (the "song" flytalk.py measures). Nothing is pre-rendered or looped. The ~190 Hz sine tone that envelope rides on, and the show names/branding, are a sonification layered on top — made up, plainly, same as this project's other demos. Captions are a genuine live decode (a cross-validated readout calibrated on the real contexts), not an echo of whichever context is driving a fly, so they can legitimately read low-confidence or as the "wrong" context.
